p.src: When Jia Zheng learned that Grandmother Jia was in grave danger, he hurried in at once to see her. He found that fright had left her breathless; Lady Wang, Yuanyang, and the others had managed to revive her and had given her pills to ease her breathing and calm her nerves. She gradually improved, though she continued to shed tears of grief. Jia Zheng tried to comfort her at her side, repeatedly saying, “Your unworthy sons have brought this disaster upon ourselves and caused you such a fright. If you can set your mind at ease, we shall still be able to attend to matters outside; but if anything should happen to you, our guilt would be heavier still.” Grandmother Jia said, “I have lived for more than eighty years. From the time I was a girl until I came into your father’s household, I have always enjoyed our ancestors’ blessings and never heard of such things. Now that I am old, how can my heart bear to see you suffer punishment? I would rather close my eyes and follow you in death.” At this, she began to weep again.

p.src: Jia Zheng was beside himself with anxiety when he heard someone outside announce, “Master, there is news from the Inner Court.” Jia Zheng hurried out and found the chief secretary of the Prince of Beijing’s household, who declared as soon as they met, “Excellent news!” Jia Zheng thanked him and invited him to sit. “May I ask what instructions His Highness has for me?” The secretary replied, “Our prince and the Prince of Xiping entered the palace to make a further report, conveying on your behalf both your apprehension and your gratitude for the grace of Heaven. His Majesty showed great compassion and, mindful that the Imperial Consort passed away only recently, could not bear to impose punishment. By special grace, you are to continue serving as an assistant director in the Ministry of Works. Of the confiscated family property, only Jia She’s share is to be forfeited to the state; all the rest is to be returned. An edict has also been issued ordering you to discharge your duties with utmost devotion. Only the loan contracts seized in the search have been entrusted to our prince for examination. Any that violate the law by charging exorbitant interest will be forfeited to the state in accordance with regulations, while those bearing the prescribed rate of interest, together with the deeds to houses and land, will all be returned. Jia Lian is to be stripped of his official rank, but pardoned and released.” When Jia Zheng had heard everything, he immediately rose and kowtowed in gratitude for the imperial favor, then bowed his thanks for the prince’s kindness. “May I ask you, Chief Secretary, to convey my thanks for now. Tomorrow morning I shall go to the palace gates to express my gratitude for His Majesty’s grace, and then come to the prince’s residence to kowtow.” The chief secretary then departed. A short while later, the edict was formally issued. In obedience to the edict, the officials in charge investigated each item: whatever was to be forfeited was taken into state ownership, and whatever was to be restored was returned. Jia Lian was released, while all the male and female servants registered under Jia She’s name were entered on official rolls and confiscated.

p.src: Poor Jia Lian! Apart from the deeds released according to the regulations and returned to him, everything in his quarters—even articles not ultimately forfeited to the state—had already been carried off by the men conducting the search, leaving only the furniture and household utensils. At first Jia Lian had feared punishment, so his release was already a great blessing; but when he remembered the possessions accumulated over the years and Xifeng’s private savings, worth no less than seventy or eighty thousand taels, all lost in a single day, how could he not grieve? Moreover, his father was still imprisoned in the Imperial Guard’s offices, while Xifeng lay critically ill; he was overwhelmed with sorrow. Then Jia Zheng summoned him with tears in his eyes and asked, “Because my official duties kept me occupied and I seldom managed the household, I placed you and your wife in charge of all its affairs. It may indeed have been difficult to remonstrate with your father over his conduct, but who was ultimately responsible for lending money at such extortionate interest? Such a thing is beneath a family of our standing. Now that the money has been confiscated, the financial loss is of little consequence; but how can we endure the infamy once word of this spreads?” Jia Lian knelt and said, “In managing the household affairs, your nephew never dared harbor the slightest selfish motive. All accounts of receipts and expenditures were recorded by Lai Da, Wu Xindeng, Dai Liang, and the others. You need only summon them and question them. In recent years the treasury has paid out more silver than it has taken in. Though none of us have made good the shortfall, we have already left many accounts elsewhere uncovered. If you ask the mistress, you will know the truth. As for these loan accounts, even I do not know where the money came from. You must ask Zhou Rui and Wang’er to learn the truth.” Jia Zheng said, “By your own account, you do not even know what went on in your own quarters, much less what happened throughout the household. I shall not question you further this time. Now that you are free, why do you not hurry out and inquire after your father’s case and that of your elder cousin Zhen?” Feeling deeply wronged, Jia Lian assented with tears in his eyes and went out. Sighing again and again, Jia Zheng thought, “My grandfather labored in the service of the throne and won distinction, earning two hereditary titles; now both branches of the family have committed offenses and lost them. Not one of these sons and nephews shows the least promise. O Heaven! O Heaven! How has the Jia family come to such utter ruin? Though by extraordinary imperial mercy our property has been returned, the expenses of the two households must naturally be combined under one roof. How can I alone possibly bear the burden? What Lian just said is even more astonishing: not only is there no silver in the treasury, but there is a deficit as well. All these years, our reputation has been nothing but an empty name. I can only reproach myself for having been so blind and foolish. If my Zhu were still alive, I would at least have a strong arm to help me. Baoyu may be grown now, but he is more useless than ever.” At this thought, he found his robe soaked with tears. Then another thought came to him: “Mother is so advanced in years, yet we sons have never managed to support her properly for even a single day; instead, we have frightened her half to death. Upon whom can I lay the blame for all these sins?”

p.src: As Jia Zheng grieved alone, a servant came to report that various relatives and friends had arrived to inquire after the family. Jia Zheng thanked them one by one and said, “This misfortune has befallen our house because I failed to discipline my nephews and the younger generation.” One of them said, “I have long known that your elder brother, the venerable Master She, conducted himself improperly, while Cousin Zhen was even more arrogant and self-indulgent. Had they merely been censured for an error in official business, their consciences would be clear; but this trouble was of their own making, and now it has implicated you too, Second Master.” Another said, “Plenty of other families have caused scandals without being impeached by a censor. If Master Zhen had not offended his friends, how could matters ever have come to this?” Another said, “The censor is not entirely to blame either. We heard that servants from your household and several country bumpkins had been making a public outcry outside. The censor, fearing that his impeachment might prove unfounded, tricked some men from this household into going to him and only then brought the matter to light. I have always thought your household treated its servants with the greatest leniency. Why, then, should such a thing have happened?” Another said, “As a rule, servants are never satisfied, however well they are maintained. I venture to say this only because everyone here today is a close friend or relative: even while you were serving away from the capital, I cannot vouch that—though you yourself have no love of money—the reports circulating outside were favorable. It was all the servants’ doing. You ought to take precautions. Although your own household has been left untouched this time, it would be extremely awkward if His Majesty were to grow suspicious of you in the future.” Alarmed by this, Jia Zheng asked, “What exactly have you gentlemen heard about my reputation?” They replied, “Though we have heard no firm evidence, people outside say that while you held office in the grain administration, you had the servants at your gate demand money.” On hearing this, Jia Zheng said, “Heaven itself can attest to my innocence. I have never dared entertain the thought of demanding money. But if the servants swagger about outside and swindle people in my name, and trouble results, it will be more than I can bear.” They said, “Being afraid will do no good now. Your only course is to investigate all the present stewards thoroughly; if you discover any servants who defy their master, punish them severely.” Jia Zheng nodded. Just then a gatekeeper entered and reported, “A man has come from your son-in-law Master Sun. He says his master has business to attend to and cannot come himself, so he sent someone to see how matters stand. He says the First Master owes him a sum of silver and wants the Second Master to repay it.” Troubled and dejected, Jia Zheng merely said, “I understand.” The visitors all sneered. “People say your relative Sun Shaozu is a scoundrel, and there is certainly some truth in it. Now that his father-in-law’s property has been confiscated, instead of coming to inquire after him and offer help, he hastens to demand money. It is truly outrageous.” Jia Zheng said, “Let us say no more about him for the moment. That marriage was a bad match arranged by my elder brother. My niece has already suffered more than enough for it, and now he has come to plague me as well.”

I fear the First Master and Master Zhen will not be able to withstand it.” Everyone said, “Second Master, you must go and appeal to the princes and ask them to find some way to retrieve the situation. Otherwise, both branches of the family will be ruined.” Jia Zheng agreed and thanked them, and they all departed.

p.src: By then it was time to light the lamps. Jia Zheng went inside to pay his respects to Grandmother Jia and found her somewhat better. Returning to his own rooms, he blamed Jia Lian and his wife for their lack of judgment: now that their moneylending at interest had come to light, the whole family was in disgrace. Only now did he see what Xifeng had been doing, and he was deeply distressed by it. But Xifeng was gravely ill, and he knew that all her belongings had been seized and carried away, leaving her heart heavy with anguish. It was not a suitable time to reproach her, so for the moment he suppressed his feelings and said nothing. The night passed without further incident. Early the next morning, Jia Zheng entered the palace to give thanks for the imperial favor. He then went to the residences of the Prince of Beijing and the Prince of Xiping to offer his respectful thanks and beg the two princes to protect his elder brother and nephew. Both princes promised to help. Jia Zheng also appealed for assistance to his colleagues and close friends.

p.src: Now Jia Lian, having learned that matters concerning his father and elder cousin were far from promising, could think of nothing to be done and had no choice but to return home. Pinger stayed beside Xifeng weeping, while Qiutong complained bitterly about Xifeng in the side room. Jia Lian came nearer and saw Xifeng barely clinging to life; however many reproaches he harbored, he could not bring himself to utter them just then. Pinger said through her tears, “Things have come to this, and what is gone cannot be recovered. With Mistress in this condition, we ought to summon another physician to treat her.” Jia Lian spat in disgust. “My own life may not be spared—why should I still concern myself with hers?” Hearing this, Xifeng opened her eyes and looked at him. Though she said nothing, her tears flowed without end. When Jia Lian had gone out, she said to Pinger, “Do not be so blind to the state of affairs. Now that things have come to such a pass, why should you still trouble yourself about me? I wish I could die this very day. All I ask is that you remember me and, after I die, raise Qiaojie to adulthood. Then even in the underworld I shall be grateful to you.” At this, Pinger burst into loud sobs. Xifeng continued, “You are an intelligent woman too. Though they have not come to accuse me, he must surely blame me. The trouble may have erupted outside the household, but had I not been greedy for money, I would have had no part in it now. Not only have all my schemes come to nothing, but after striving all my life to surpass others, I have ended up behind them all. I only bitterly regret having trusted the wrong people. I vaguely heard that the charge against Cousin Zhen concerns forcibly taking an honest man’s wife as a concubine and driving her to death when she refused. A man surnamed Zhang is implicated—think who else that could be. If this affair comes out at the trial, our Second Master will never escape involvement. How could I face anyone then? I want to die at once, yet I cannot endure the thought of swallowing gold or taking poison. And still you want to call a physician—is that not harming me in the very act of trying to care for me?” The more Pinger heard, the more wretched she felt. Reflecting that Xifeng was indeed in a desperate plight and fearing she might take her own life, Pinger could only keep close watch over her. Fortunately, Grandmother Jia knew none of the particulars. Her health had lately improved somewhat, and seeing that Jia Zheng was safe and that Baoyu and Baochai remained constantly at her side, she felt a little reassured. As Xifeng had always been her dearest favorite, she told Yuanyang, “Take some of my private belongings to that girl Feng, and give Pinger some silver as well. Tell her to look after Feng properly; I shall make further arrangements in due course.” She also instructed Lady Wang to look after Lady Xing. Moreover, the Ning mansion itself was confiscated by the authorities; all its property, houses, land, and household servants were entered in registers and seized. Grandmother Jia therefore sent carriages to bring Lady You, her daughters-in-law, and the others over. Pitifully, of the once-magnificent Ning mansion there now remained only Lady You and her daughter-in-law, together with Peifeng and Xieluan—not a single servant was left to them. Grandmother Jia assigned them a house to live in, directly adjoining Xichun’s quarters. She also assigned four elderly women and two maids to wait on them.

p.src: All their meals and daily necessities were apportioned and sent from the main kitchen. Grandmother Jia provided their clothes and other belongings, while incidental expenses were paid through the accounts office, each person receiving the same monthly allowance as in the Rong mansion. Jia She, Jia Zhen, and Jia Rong were being held at the Imperial Guard Office, yet the accounts office truly had no funds from which to meet their expenses. Xifeng now possessed nothing at all, while Jia Lian was burdened with debts besides. Jia Zheng understood nothing of household affairs and merely said that he had already entrusted the matter to others and that the prisoners would naturally be looked after. At his wits’ end, Jia Lian considered their relatives. Aunt Xue’s household was already ruined, Wang Ziteng was dead, and though other kinsmen remained, none was able to help. He therefore secretly sent men to their rural estate to sell some land temporarily, raising several thousand taels for expenses in prison. Once Jia Lian resorted to this measure, the household servants, seeing their masters’ fortunes in decline, took the opportunity to practice their own deceits, even appropriating some of the rents and taxes from the eastern estate under various pretexts. But that belongs to a later part of the story and need not be told for now.

p.src: Now the Lady Dowager saw that the hereditary offices of their ancestors had been revoked, that her descendants were being held in prison for interrogation, that Lady Xing, Madam You, and the others wept day and night, and that Xifeng lay gravely ill. Though Baoyu and Baochai remained at her side, they could only offer words of comfort and could not share her burden. Thus she knew no peace by day or night; as she brooded over the past and future, her tears never dried. One evening she sent Baoyu away, struggled into a sitting position, and told Yuanyang and the others to burn incense in all the family shrines. She also ordered a tall spiral of incense to be lit in her own courtyard, then leaned on her cane and made her way outside. Amber understood that the old lady meant to worship the Buddha and spread out a small bright-red felt prayer mat. The Lady Dowager offered incense, knelt down, and repeatedly knocked her head upon the ground. After invoking the Buddha for some time, she tearfully prayed to Heaven and Earth: “Supreme Heaven and merciful Bodhisattvas above, I, a daughter of the Shi family married into the Jia house, pray to you in all sincerity and implore the Bodhisattvas to show compassion. For generations, our Jia family has never dared to commit violence or abuse its power. I have supported my husband and helped my sons; though I may not have done good, neither have I dared to do evil. It must be that the younger generations have grown arrogant, extravagant, violent, and dissolute, wantonly wasting Heaven’s gifts, and so brought about the search and confiscation of the entire household. Now that my sons and grandsons are imprisoned, they naturally face far more peril than hope. All this is due to my own sins, for I failed to instruct my descendants, and that is why matters have come to this. p.src: The weeping throughout the room was loud enough to shake heaven and earth. It terrified the old women keeping watch outside, and one of them hurried to inform Jia Zheng. Jia Zheng was sitting gloomily in his study. When the messenger from the Lady Dowager arrived, he grew alarmed and rushed into the inner apartments. Hearing so many people weeping from afar, he supposed that something had happened to the old lady and was nearly frightened out of his wits. He hurried in, but when he saw her sitting there alive and weeping, his senses returned. He said, “When the old lady is grieving, you ought to comfort her. Why have you all joined together in weeping?” At the sound of Jia Zheng’s voice, everyone hastily stopped crying and stared blankly at one another. Jia Zheng stepped forward to console the Lady Dowager, then reproved the others with a few words. Each of them thought, “We came precisely because we feared the old lady would grieve and meant to comfort her. How did we lose control and all end up weeping bitterly ourselves?” While they were still perplexed, an old servant woman led in two women from the household of Marquis Shi. After paying their respects to the Lady Dowager and greeting everyone else, they said, “Our master, mistress, and young lady sent us here. They have heard that what happened in your household is really nothing very serious, but only a passing fright. They were afraid that your master and mistress might be distressed, so they told us to come and let you know that your Second Master here is no longer in danger. Our young lady had intended to come herself, but as she is to be married in only a few days, she was unable to do so.” The Lady Dowager heard them out and, unable in the circumstances to express her thanks properly, said, “Give them my regards when you return. It is the destiny of our family that matters should be so. I am grateful that your master and mistress have kept us in their thoughts. I shall thank them properly another day. Since your young lady is to marry, I assume there can be no fault to find with the bridegroom. What are his family’s circumstances?” The two women replied, “His family’s means are nothing remarkable, but the bridegroom is very handsome and has a mild and peaceable nature. We have seen him several times. He appears much like Second Master Bao here, and we have also heard that he possesses both talent and learning.” The Lady Dowager was pleased to hear this and said, “We are all southerners. Though we have lived here a long time, we still follow southern custom in such important matters, so none of us has seen the new bridegroom. Only the other day I was thinking of my own family. Of all of them, your young lady is the one I love best. Out of the three hundred and sixty days in a year, she spent more than two hundred at my side, and that is how she grew up. I had meant to find her a worthy husband myself, but since her uncle was away from home, it was not proper for me to make the decision. Since good fortune has granted her a fine husband, my mind is at ease. When she marries this month, I had intended to come and drink a cup of wedding wine. But now such trouble has erupted in our family that my heart feels as if it were being scorched in a boiling pan. How could I possibly go to your house?”

p.src: Go back and convey my regards, and say that everyone here sends their greetings and good wishes. And be sure to tell your young mistress not to worry about me. I am over eighty now, and even if I die, no one could say I have not been blessed. I only pray that once she is married, husband and wife will live in harmony and grow old together; then I shall be at peace.” As she spoke, tears began to fall despite herself. The woman said, “You need not grieve, Old Madam. After our young mistress is married and the ninth-day observance is over, she and her husband will surely come to pay their respects. How delighted you will be to see them then!” Grandmother Jia nodded. The woman withdrew. No one else paid much attention, but Baoyu listened in a daze for a while and thought, “Life grows more unbearable with every passing day. Why must people marry off their daughters once they have raised them to adulthood, and why must the girls change as soon as they marry? Even someone like Cousin Shi has been forced by her uncle into a match, and when she sees me in future, she too will surely ignore me. When a person has reached the point where no one cares for him, what is the use of going on living?” At this thought, sorrow overcame him once more. Seeing that Grandmother Jia had only just recovered her composure, he dared not weep and merely sat there in dejection.

p.src: After a while, Jia Zheng, still uneasy, came in again to see the Old Madam. Finding her somewhat better, he went out and summoned Lai Da, ordering him to bring the register of all the household stewards and servants in the mansion. When they were counted together, and those belonging to Jia She's confiscated establishment were excluded, there remained more than thirty families, comprising two hundred and twelve men and women. Jia Zheng summoned the twenty-one men currently serving in the mansion and questioned them about the household accounts over the years—how much income had come in and how much expenditure ought to have gone out. The servant in overall charge presented the recent account book of disbursements. When Jia Zheng examined it, he found that income fell short of expenditure; added to the expenses incurred year after year for the palace, there were also many unsecured loans recorded as having been raised outside. He next checked the rents from the eastern province and found that recent remittances were less than half what they had been in his ancestors' time, while current expenses had risen to ten times their former level. Jia Zheng might have remained calm had he not looked, but once he had seen the figures, he stamped his foot in alarm and cried, “This is disastrous! I supposed that although Lian was managing affairs, he must have kept the household under control. Little did I know that for years we had already been spending next year's income this year, all merely to keep up appearances! Treating the stipend of our hereditary office as though it were of no consequence—how could the family not come to ruin? Even if I begin economizing now, it is already too late.” At this thought he paced back and forth with his hands clasped behind his back, utterly at a loss. The others knew that Jia Zheng had no understanding of household management and was merely worrying himself to no purpose, so they said, “There is no need for you to distress yourself, sir. Every great household is like this. If everything were reckoned together, even a prince's household would find its income insufficient. One simply keeps up appearances and carries on for as long as one can. After all, it was through His Majesty's grace that you retained even this small portion of the family property. If all of it had been confiscated, would you simply have ceased living?” Jia Zheng snapped, “Nonsense! You heartless pack of slaves squander whatever you please while your masters prosper; when everything is gone, some of you leave and others run away. Would any of you care whether your masters lived or died? You think it fortunate that our property was not sealed and confiscated, but you know nothing of our reputation outside. The very foundation of the family is in peril, yet you still put on airs outside, boast, deceive, and swindle people; when trouble breaks out, you think you can settle everything merely by shifting the blame onto your masters. As for the present cases involving the Elder Master and Master Zhen, it is said that news of them was spread outside by our servant Bao Er. Yet I see no Bao Er in this register. How do you explain that?” They replied, “Bao Er is not entered in the registers. He was formerly listed with the Ning mansion, but the Second Master found him honest and brought him and his wife over here. After his wife died, he returned to the Ning mansion.
